disclaimer: Generation figures are long-run averages for a well-oriented, unshaded rooftop array. Prices are indicative all-in installed costs for ALMM-listed modules with a standard structure and net meter; actual quotes vary by roof type, structure height, cable runs, brand and state.

subsidy.scheme: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana

groupHousing.note: Common facilities of Group Housing Societies / RWAs — EV charging, lifts, lighting, water pumps.

conditions: Residential consumers only; the electricity connection must be in the applicant's name.
Grid-connected system with a net meter; off-grid systems are not eligible.
Installation must be done by a vendor registered on the National Portal.
Modules and cells must be from the ALMM approved list; DCR cells are required.
Subsidy is credited directly to the applicant's bank account, typically within about 30 days of installation, inspection and net-meter commissioning.

stateTopUp.note: ₹10,000/kW capital subsidy capped at ₹30,000 (3 kW), plus a generation-based incentive of ₹3/kWh up to 3 kW and ₹2/kWh for 3–10 kW, via the Delhi Solar Portal.
State subsidy for residential rooftop up to 3 kW.
Additional support targeted at Antyodaya households rather than a general per-kW top-up.
Central subsidy only; Gujarat's Surya Gujarat framework routes through the same national portal.

systemTypes.name: On-grid (grid-tied)
pros: Eligible for PM Surya Ghar subsidy
cons: Shuts down during a power cut
systemTypes.bestFor: Cities and towns with reliable supply — the default choice for ~85% of homes.

systemTypes.name: Hybrid (solar + battery)
pros: Subsidy applies to the solar portion
cons: Battery adds roughly ₹35,000–60,000 per usable kWh installed
systemTypes.bestFor: Areas with frequent or long outages, or homes replacing a diesel/inverter setup.

systemTypes.name: Off-grid
pros: Works with no grid connection at all
cons: Not eligible for the central subsidy
systemTypes.bestFor: Farmhouses, remote sites and properties with no reliable connection.
